local_scope: Skimmed content/the-right-to-counsel index and node pages; existence checked against content/cases/, _overhaul2/lake/_manifest.json, _run/s6-candidates/r7-queue-batch1.jsonl, and _run/s6-candidates/gated.jsonl before rows were kept.
inclusion_floor: page_candidate true only for missing controlling SCOTUS, binding-in-circuit omitted-question authority, or split-marker authority with both sides/circuits named; historical, fact-bound, or subsumed real finds are mention-only.
remit: Officer field conduct, admissibility/suppression, and officer civil liability only; trial-craft-only right-to-counsel cases were excluded.
source_crosscheck: SCOTUS candidates cross-checked through non-CourtListener web sources, usually Supreme Justia plus LOC U.S. Reports PDF or Cornell LII.

caption: Kansas v. Ventris
justification: Missing controlling Massiah remedy/admissibility case: a statement concededly elicited by a jailhouse informant in violation of the Sixth Amendment is excluded from the prosecution's case-in-chief but may be used to impeach the defendant's inconsistent testimony.

caption: United States v. Morrison
justification: Missing controlling remedy case for post-charge government-agent interference with counsel: even assuming a Sixth Amendment violation from DEA agents meeting a represented indicted defendant without counsel, dismissal is inappropriate absent demonstrable prejudice or a substantial threat of prejudice; remedy must be tailored to the injury.

caption: Weatherford v. Bursey
justification: Missing controlling officer-civil-liability/adverse boundary case: an undercover agent's presence at defense meetings did not create a per se Sixth Amendment violation where he did not seek or transmit defense strategy and attended to preserve his cover, rejecting automatic liability/new-trial rules for all attorney-client intrusions.

caption: Moore v. Illinois
justification: Missing controlling post-attachment identification case for the draft lineup node: a corporeal one-on-one identification at a preliminary hearing after adversary proceedings began violated the Sixth Amendment when conducted without counsel, and the State could not use the direct pretrial-identification testimony merely by showing an independent source.

caption: Michigan v. Harvey
justification: Mention-only. Real Sixth Amendment impeachment/remedy authority for statements taken in violation of the now-overruled Michigan v. Jackson prophylactic rule; live teaching value is historical/background because Montejo overruled Jackson and Ventris is the cleaner current Massiah-impeachment authority.

caption: Black v. United States
justification: Mention-only. Real attorney-client eavesdropping remand, but fact-bound/per curiam and better handled as background to Weatherford and Morrison rather than a standalone page candidate in this category.

caption: O'Brien v. United States
justification: Mention-only. Real post-indictment eavesdropping remand following Black, but terse/per curiam and subsumed by Weatherford/Morrison for the operative intrusion/remedy rule.
